active_paradigms.idea: Replace the final physical-expert-to-GPU LPT packing with a per-layer minimax mixed-integer linear program using scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program first greedily chooses replica counts, then uses cardinality-constrained LPT twice: groups to nodes and physical replicas to GPUs. Its strongest feature is that it reduces each decision to independent per-row packing, so it is fast and produces valid exact-capacity placements. Its principal weakness is that LPT plus one swap is only a local heuristic: the one allowed swap considers only the currently lightest and heaviest pack, cannot make a coordinated cycle of moves, and can miss substantially better assignments. Keep the existing group-to-node and replica-count construction, but replace Step 3 with one scipy.optimize.milp call independently for each layer/node. Create binary variables x[p,g] for assigning each already-created physical replica p to each local GPU g, enforce one GPU per replica and exactly phy_experts_per_gpu replicas per GPU, and add a continuous makespan variable z with sum_p replica_load[p]*x[p,g] <= z for every GPU. Minimize z, using scipy.optimize.Bounds and scipy.optimize.LinearConstraint, and recover the permutation/rank tensors from the binary solution. This directly optimizes the bottleneck that LPT is attempting to approximate while preserving the current output contract and hierarchical node locality.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary balance quality: minimize the maximum per-GPU replica load after replication, especially adversarial rows where a single swap cannot repair LPT. Use it only when the local replica count is small enough that solve time remains below the evaluator timeout.
active_paradigms.cautions: The provided wrapper does not expose the original evaluator's combined-score formula, so validate whether it scores maximum load, imbalance range, and runtime before committing. Solve independently per layer and node; a global MILP is unnecessarily large. Set integrality=1 only on assignment variables, give z a nonnegative continuous bound, use a finite time_limit if supported, and fall back to the present LPT result if the solver returns no feasible incumbent. Do not alter phy2log/phyrank semantics: only reorder existing physical replicas, then rebuild inverse permutations exactly as the current code does.

active_paradigms.idea: Use networkx.min_cost_flow for a convex-cost replica-placement formulation rather than greedy heap packing
active_paradigms.description: Model each local packing stage as a single min-cost-flow graph whose flow units are physical replica items and whose sink-side parallel arcs represent progressively more expensive capacity on each GPU. The current LPT method greedily commits a large replica before seeing which later replicas must fill the remaining fixed slots; its one extreme swap repairs only one pair and therefore does not capture coordinated reassignment. Construct a source-to-replica arc of capacity one, replica-to-GPU-slot arcs of capacity one, and GPU-slot-to-sink arcs whose increasing marginal costs encode the desired load-balancing penalty around the target local average. Set the replica-to-slot costs from each replica's post-replication load times that slot's marginal penalty, then call networkx.min_cost_flow once. The resulting integral flow supplies a valid exact-cardinality GPU assignment without a custom heap or local-search loop. This is particularly attractive if the evaluator rewards broad distribution rather than only the single maximum, because convex slot costs discourage concentration across all GPUs. Use the existing hierarchy and greedy replication allocation initially, so the graph only replaces the final physical placement decision.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce global per-GPU load spread and tail imbalance with a polynomial-time integral optimization, while avoiding the potentially variable runtime of a full MILP.
active_paradigms.cautions: Min-cost flow has a linear arc-cost objective, not an exact max-load objective; choose marginal slot penalties to approximate the evaluator's imbalance metric and compare against LPT on representative workload rows. Costs should be scaled to integers because NetworkX flow implementations are most reliable with integer demands/costs; preserve ordering deterministically for ties. The graph can grow as replicas times GPUs times slots, so apply it per layer/node and retain LPT for unusually large instances. Exact fixed replica counts must be enforced by the number of GPU-slot arcs, not merely by soft costs.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment as an exact assignment solver for targeted group-to-node repair around the current hierarchical layout
active_paradigms.description: The hierarchy currently packs groups by their total load before it knows how much replication will later be needed inside each node. Consequently, a node can receive a mix whose aggregate group total looks balanced but whose concentrated hot experts consume many local replica slots and leave a worse achievable GPU makespan. Retain the current group ordering as a baseline, compute a per-group pressure score such as its predicted local bottleneck after the deterministic replica rule, and build a square cost matrix between group positions and node-specific group slots. The cost for placing group q into a node slot should include its pressure plus a deterministic penalty for moving it away from its original node, thereby allowing only beneficial cross-node changes. Call scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment once per layer to obtain a globally consistent reassignment of groups to node slots, then run the unchanged replication and local GPU packer. This differs from changing the GPU packer: it improves the upstream partition that determines which experts are even allowed to share replica capacity. It can be much faster than MILP because assignment is cubic in group count and has predictable runtime.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve hierarchical balance by reducing node-level hot-expert concentration before replica allocation; preserve or improve execution time relative to multi-swap local search or MILP.
active_paradigms.cautions: Linear assignment optimizes additive placement costs, so the pressure score must be derived carefully from the actual replica-allocation bottleneck rather than raw group token sum alone. The current code requires each node to receive exactly groups_per_node contiguous logical-group slots; preserve this cardinality and reconstruct log2mlog/mlog2log consistently. If the evaluator penalizes movement or requires stable mappings across invocations, increase the movement penalty and deterministic tie breaking. Because the actual evaluator formula is absent from the shown wrapper, benchmark raw-load pressure, max-expert pressure, and predicted replica-load pressure rather than assuming one is correct.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace LPT packing with an exact cardinality-constrained minimax MILP for the small per-layer packing subproblems
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first applies LPT to assign fixed-size groups to nodes and physical replicas to GPUs, then considers only one swap between the globally lightest and heaviest packs. This is fast, but it can leave large improvements requiring a coordinated cycle of several moves or a swap involving non-extreme packs. Formulate each call to `balanced_packing` as a minimax binary assignment model solved by `scipy.optimize.milp`: binary variable x[i,p] means item i is assigned to pack p, every item is assigned once, every pack receives exactly `groups_per_pack` items, and each pack load is constrained to be at most a scalar makespan T. Minimize T directly, using integrality=1 and sparse `LinearConstraint` matrices. Use this only below a conservative size threshold, such as at most 32 items or a modest variable budget; retain the present LPT implementation for larger instances. The model is especially attractive for the group-to-node stage because group counts are usually much smaller than the number of replicas and this stage determines the topology-locality ceiling for all later decisions. For the GPU stage, solve the MILP only when there are few GPUs per node, where exact packing can materially improve the worst GPU load at negligible total evaluator cost. Reconstruct `pack_index` from selected variables and assign `rank_in_pack` deterministically by sorted original item index, preserving all map-shape and rank invariants.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce maximum node and GPU load directly rather than merely reducing the range of the current LPT solution; this targets the likely dominant load-balance component of the scalar score while retaining a fast fallback for runtime-sensitive large cases.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The shown adapter exposes only `combined_score`, not the original evaluator's component formula, so validate MILP thresholds against the real evaluator rather than assuming exact optimization always wins after solver overhead. Set a strict per-instance `time_limit`, accept only solver solutions with a valid integral assignment, and fall back to LPT on timeout or non-success. Do not formulate all layers jointly: layers are independent in the current output contract, and a joint model would be unnecessarily expensive. Keep all tensors CPU/int64 and ensure exactly one rank is emitted for every slot in each pack.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a slot-expanded linear assignment to globally repair GPU placement after replication
tried_paradigms.description: The current second packing stage treats every replica as an independent item and LPT assigns it greedily to GPU packs with a one-pair swap. Instead, create one column per physical GPU slot and solve `scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` over replicas versus slots. Construct the cost matrix from the load of each replica and a target per-GPU load: assigning a heavier replica to a slot belonging to a currently under-target GPU receives lower cost, while assignment to an over-target GPU receives a convex overload penalty. Include deterministic tiny tie-break terms based on GPU and original physical index so mappings are stable. Each GPU has exactly `phy_experts_per_gpu` duplicated slot columns, therefore the assignment automatically preserves the hard equal-expert-count constraint without any custom repair. This is a fundamentally broader move than the present extreme swap: one assignment call can permute every physical expert among all GPU slots simultaneously. Apply it independently within each node in hierarchical mode, so no replica crosses the node selected by the first-stage group packing. For global mode it naturally operates over all GPUs. Decode the assigned column into GPU index and rank, then use the existing inverse-permutation and logical-map reconstruction unchanged.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve the final per-GPU imbalance and remove local minima caused by LPT plus a single extreme-pair swap, while preserving the exact number of physical experts per GPU and topology constraints.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Linear assignment minimizes separable assignment costs, whereas true GPU load imbalance is coupled; the target and convex cost must be chosen from the replica-load total, not from the original logical loads. A dense replica-by-slot matrix can be too large, so use this only when `num_physical_experts` is moderate and retain current packing otherwise. The cost must not accidentally reward putting several heavy replicas onto the same GPU merely because its duplicated columns have identical costs; encode a distinct marginal overload cost for the first, second, and later slot of a GPU. Do not change `phyrank`: it remains the replica rank associated with the logical expert, independent of its assigned GPU slot.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use min-cost flow with marginal GPU-load arcs to make replication placement topology-aware
tried_paradigms.description: The key structural weakness is that replication and placement are optimized separately: `replicate_experts` greedily minimizes individual replica load within a node, then packing tries to place the resulting fixed replicas. Replace the placement decision with a discretized convex transportation model solved in one `networkx.network_simplex` call per layer/node. Create a source-to-expert supply arc for every required physical copy, expert-to-GPU arcs for legal GPUs in that node, and GPU-to-sink arcs representing expert slots. Give successive GPU capacity arcs increasing marginal costs based on projected load, so the min-cost-flow objective approximates squared load or a sharp penalty above average load. Expert-to-GPU arcs can additionally carry a locality-aware cost: zero within the group-selected node and prohibitively large or absent across nodes. Supply one unit for each physical replica slot, making both replica counts and GPU capacity exact integer constraints in the flow model. Decode the units leaving each expert into the needed `phy2log` entries and assign replica ranks consecutively, then build `logcnt` and `log2phy` exactly as in the current implementation. This permits the flow objective to decide where the extra copies of a hot expert are useful rather than committing all copy choices before seeing GPU capacities. It is particularly promising when a few very hot experts interact with uneven group/node totals, where independent greedy replication commonly over-concentrates the wrong logical experts within a node.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Jointly reduce GPU overload and replica-induced hotspots under exact node locality and fixed physical-slot constraints; this addresses the coupling that the current greedy replication plus LPT decomposition cannot see.
tried_paradigms.cautions: `networkx.network_simplex` requires integral demands, capacities, and costs, so scale floating loads to bounded integers carefully and use deterministic rounding; overflow or excessively large scales can make it slow. The convex load objective is an approximation through marginal-cost arcs, so choose a small number of load quanta and fall back to the current method if the graph would be large. Preserve the required total number of replicas and never allow an expert to receive zero copies. If the evaluator expects the hierarchical group-to-node policy, restrict arcs to the selected node rather than allowing globally cheaper cross-node placement.
